claim: C. briggsae and C. elegans diverged by 15-30 million years.

claim: In C. elegans, the switch gene sdc-2 sets the sex determination pathway to the hermaphrodite mode in XX embryos.
source: For example, in XX embryos, the switch gene sdc-2 sets the sex determination pathway to the hermaphrodite mode and triggers the binding of a DCC onto both X chromosomes to reduce X gene expression by half and thereby match X expression with that from XO males (Meyer, 2022a).
evidence: Supported by citation to Meyer, 2022a

claim: In C. elegans, sdc-2 triggers the binding of a DCC onto both X chromosomes to reduce X gene expression by half.

evidence: Supported by citation to Meyer, 2022a

claim: Three sex-determination genes required for C. elegans hermaphrodite sexual differentiation but not dosage compensation, tra-1, tra-2, and tra-3, are conserved between C. elegans and C. briggsae and play very similar roles.

Mutation of any one gene causes virtually identical masculinizing somatic and germline phenotypes in both species (Kelleher et al., 2008).

claim: Extrachromosomal arrays made in C. briggsae with Cel rex sites failed to bind the Cbr DCC or titrate it from the Cbr X.

claim: 100% of extrachromosomal arrays made in C. elegans with DNA from either Cel rex-33 or Cel rex-4 recruited the Cel DCC.

claim: Insertion of Cel rex-32 into a new location on X resulted in DCC binding that was not significantly different from binding at its endogenous location on X.

claim: All Cbr rex sites except rex-1 failed to recruit the Cel DCC when inserted into Cel X chromosomes.

claim: MEX is enriched up to 12-fold on X chromosomes versus autosomes.

claim: MEX II is enriched up to 30-fold on X versus autosomes.
source: A 13 bp motif named MEX (Motif Enriched on X) is enriched up to 12-fold on X chromosomes versus autosomes, and a 30 bp motif named MEX II is enriched up to 30-fold on X versus autosomes (Figure 7A and B).

claim: In C. elegans, two motifs are highly enriched on X chromosomes relative to autosomes: a 12 bp motif also called MEX and a 26 bp motif called MEX II.

claim: The CAGGG core is necessary but not sufficient for DCC binding in C. elegans.

claim: The C. elegans consensus MEX motif predominantly has a cytosine nucleotide located two nucleotides 5' to the core CAGGG sequence.

claim: In C. elegans, a 9 bp motif called Motif C also participates in Cel DCC recruitment to X but lacks enrichment on X.

claim: C. elegans Motif C fails to participate in Cbr DCC recruitment to Cbr X chromosomes.
